high_level_description: Wordless Bayeux-inspired embroidery: a narrow blue workflow band is sealed inside a rigid wooden guide before an operator turns the loom and produces one finished panel below, while a disconnected red revision waits in an unused cradle for a later run; flat wool figures on linen, no text or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A single undyed linen field is divided into three stacked registers by narrow stitched borders of leaves and ordinary workshop animals. The upper register contains the sealing gesture, the middle contains the operating mechanism, and the lower contains the finished result and the future revision. All three remain visible at once. No inscription, letter, numeral, heraldic badge, pointing hand, caption, diagram, or directional mark appears anywhere.

elements.desc: Single tall execution loom built from ochre timber, spanning the upper and middle registers. One narrow blue wool workflow band runs straight downward inside a rigid lidded guide with small viewing slits and no hand-sized opening. A single red wax seal crosses the closed lid; only one external crank projects from the right side.

Workflow author shown in flat profile, medium-brown skin, short dark curls, cream tunic, indigo mantle, ochre shoes, and a concentrated expression. Kneeling in the upper-left register, they have just pressed the only wax seal across the guide lid; both empty hands are now withdrawn and remain outside the loom mechanism.

Execution operator shown in flat profile, dark skin, close-cropped black hair, indigo tunic, cream leggings, red shoes, and a steady neutral expression. Standing in the middle-right register, he turns the single external crank with both hands. The sealed guide remains above and beyond his reach, with no second handle, hatch, or editing tool.

Single completed repair panel emerging directly from the loom's lower slot into the lower-left register. The cream woven rectangle has a blue border and a compact arrangement of purely pictorial hand-tool silhouettes. Its upper edge remains visibly aligned with the narrow blue band, while its surface carries no writing, number, seal, badge, or arrow.

Separate red wool revision roll resting inside its own unused wooden preparation cradle in the lower-right register, treated as one unified object. A plain cream cord binds the roll and one changed junction is visible in its weave. A wide empty gap separates the cradle from the operating loom, with no thread, belt, opening, or shared mechanism.
